What I would test next

I can follow the links and get back to the call in this prototype. I still need to see whether that helps a developer understand the change.

Give both screens the same task

Ask developers to explain the workspace-access check and inspect its guard. Use Unified on both screens, with the same commit, task and available content. Change which screen they try first so the second attempt does not always benefit from familiarity.

Watch for wrong turns, missed branches and time spent finding their place. Ask them to explain what the code does, rather than only timing the clicks.

Check what the highlight might hide

Start from code and ask what the summary might miss. A small highlight could make someone stop looking too soon. If people inspect less context or miss more branches, the links need to change even if navigation is faster.

Check the cases this sample leaves out

Try a modified file with meaningful code on both sides, a larger code font, and a new commit that moves or removes a linked range. The interface should explain an outdated link and let the reviewer open the relevant version or file.

Earlier explorations

Behavior-first, counterexamples, impact-first and author handoff remain in Paper’s exploration archive. They change the review model or require additional information. M keeps the layer model and focuses this submission on the existing reviewing screen.
